findings.title: The obs116.py rows check is blind to frames missing from all three streams
findings.evidence:
obs116.py:386-388 builds `ns` only from the n values it actually saw (n >= stable) and sets `missing = len(ns) - len(good)`. A frame whose FrameTrace, FrameTrace-draw and FrameTrace-x lines are all absent is never in `ns`, so it is neither counted as missing nor refused. It would only drop silently out of every sum.

This run is not affected: my recount finds n = 432..9929 contiguous (9 498 of 9 498).

result.severity_if_real: MAJOR. It sets the direction of session 117: T1 was picked over T2 and AheadTake on a ceiling that the code and this run's counters rule out. The damage is limited by item 6's own bar: the multi-entry memo is built only if the census shows at least 1 ms a frame. result.reasoning:
I could not refute F1. I rechecked the code and recounted every number from C:/kyty/s116/log_obs116.txt myself (binary read, rows with n >= 432 that have all three FrameTrace lines). Scratch files are in C:/kyty/s116/audit116/skeptic_f1/ (rec.py, arr.npy, pc.cpp).

**Recounted numbers: all CONFIRMED**
- 9 498 rows.
- pmemo_hit 6 812.31 and pmemo_miss 2 206.00 a frame; 9 018.3 lookups; 1.7652 per mh_draw; miss share 24.46 %.
- pmemo_chk_us 433.29.
- da_take_us 3 002.48 a frame, which is 44.74 % of mh_prog (6 711.42).
- Model 1: mh_prog = -712.7 + 0.7530 x stages + 0.2872 (+-0.026) x misses, R2 0.9498.
- Model 2, adding da_take: miss premium 0.2030 +- 0.0138, R2 0.9859.
- Collinearity between stages and misses: correlation 0.9145, VIF 6.11.
- The most generous attribution, mh_prog minus da_take minus chk, is 3 275.7 us = 48.8 %.
- Session 86's price: 699 / (0.75 x 9 122.7) = 0.102 us per converted stage, times 2 206 = 0.225 ms.
- Session 86 text also CONFIRMED: K_miss 73.79 ns, K_hit 14.53 ns, and -699.0 +- 86.3 us for progmemo=1.
- Session 83 wrote that the lock and ProgramCache::Get run on every draw regardless of the memo. CONFIRMED.

**Code: CONFIRMED**
- Source is unchanged since 7c73f26: `git diff 7c73f26 HEAD -- src` is empty.
- pipelineCache.cpp:4868-4872 counts per stage (VS +1, PS +1 only when pixel_active). videoOut.cpp:1785-1792 prints the counters.
- A memo hit skips only PrepareProgram (shader.cpp:969 and :1102; the finding says 1101), MemoRecord (4222-4250), and BuildStageStaticKey plus programs.find (3489-3511).
- AheadNote/AheadTake (3589-3614) and MaterializeResources are gated on `entry != end` and the stage, not on key_hit, so hits pay them too.
- The pipeline memo at 5283-5288 does not depend on a stage hit, so a miss adds nothing outside mh_prog.

**Why "most of 6.7 ms" cannot hold**
Most of 6.7 ms spread over 2 206 misses means at least 1.52 us a miss. The whole of mh_prog averages 0.744 us a lookup. Even charging misses with everything hits do not provably pay gives 3.28 ms, which is 48.8 %, still below half.

Session 86's own split is tighter still. Everything before the lock (pg_pre, 1 541 us) plus key and find (pg_key, 255 us) came to about 30 % of mh_prog.

Within-bucket checks agree:
- Slopes of mh_prog on misses inside stage buckets are noisy and small; their weighted mean is 0.08 us.
- Draw buckets likewise stay mostly well under 1.5 us a miss (-0.70 to 0.41), except one noisy 121-row bucket at 2.0.

**Minor imprecisions in F1 (none change the conclusion)**
- PS PrepareProgram is at shader.cpp:1102, not 1101.
- Session 87's 63.1 % is AheadTake's share of the Get block without key and find. pg_ahead / pg_get is 59.5 %.

**Caveat on F1's prediction**
The ceiling correction is solid; the prediction that the census falls under 1 ms is less certain. The mis-specified model with mh_draws instead of stages gives 0.69 us a miss, 1.53 ms if every miss were caught. That model is wrong for per-stage counters, and even 1.53 ms is not "most of 6.7 ms". The fix should record the bound as roughly 0.2-0.65 ms, with at most about 2 ms from session 86's pre-lock plus key split.

result.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. I checked every claim against the files, and the finding if anything understates the problem.

1. Item 1 (г) required both timings. ROADMAP.md lines 2001-2002 say "(г) замер `--no-memo` на `ttl114b` полный и выборочный". The finding cites line 2003, which is only the next line; that slip is harmless. `next-session-116.md:29` also says "(d) timings with --no-memo on ttl114b (full and selected)". CONFIRMED.

2. The workflow dropped the full timing. `audit116/protocol/workflow_v41_script.js` shows the build's (d) became "keep every v4 guarantee". Its acceptance asks for only two ttl114b runs: item 1 is the selected run with `--no-memo`, and item 2 is the same run with the memo on. There is no full `--no-memo` run. The workflow started at 14:51:25Z, which is 16:51:25 local time. No ROADMAP item records this change, although item 1 of the session-115 rules requires "каждое изменение запущенного воркфлоу — сначала в ROADMAP". CONFIRMED.

3. No full `--no-memo` ttl114b run exists anywhere.
   - `accept41/out/heavy/` has only `h1_nomemo`, `h2_memo` and a dry run, all of the 185 selected mutants.
   - `v41check/out/heavy/` has only `ttl114b_sel`.
   - The only full ttl114b run is `v4check/out/heavy/b1_6118aef5/full_warm`. Its header shows mutlib sha 6118aef5 and the memo on (read_run memo, dep hash 02ba6baa…). Wall 1 220.1 s, worker time 30 258 s.
   - `ACCEPTANCE_V41.md` lines 93-94 say "(not measured; the full v4 run with the memo took 20.3 min)".
   - `ACCEPTANCE_V4.md` lines 37 and 118 say "1 220 s (20.3 min, build 6118aef5, warm)".
   
   CONFIRMED.

4. Item 5 rests on the unmeasured number.
   - ROADMAP lines 2053 and 2058-2061 allow only full runs with `--control --no-memo` and say memo caches stay off on sealed copies.
   - The same item states "ABBA-печать ≈ 20 мин (было ~70) — практический уровень" and stops speed work on that basis.
   - Line 2053 puts "полный v4 — 20,3 мин" next to the `--no-memo` number, so a memo-on warm figure reads as if it were the permitted mode.
   - Commit ceec841 repeats "~20 min per ABBA seal".
   
   CONFIRMED.

5. My own estimate says the real cost is about twice 20 min.
   - I matched job times for the 185 mutants that appear in both reports: `h1_nomemo` (v4.1, `--no-memo`) against `full_warm` (v4, memo on).
   - `--no-memo` jobs take 2.49× as long in total (median ratio per mutant 2.70). The baselines agree: 685 s against 298 s.
   - I scaled the other 160 mutants from `full_warm` by the same factor. That gives about 71 300 s of mutant time. Adding baselines and controls (3 224 s) gives about 74 500 s of worker time. Over 28 workers that is at least about 2 660 s, roughly 44 min of wall.
   - Correcting for the ×1.14 hot-memo difference between the two runs (a game was loading the machine during the v4.1 runs) still leaves about 39 min.
   
   So a ttl114b-size seal in the permitted mode probably takes about 40-45 min, not about 20. Stopping speed work at "practical level" rests on a number that is wrong by roughly half.

6. Precedent and suite sizes.
   - The v3 net112 `--no-memo` run took 2 016.7 s (33.6 min); `ACCEPTANCE_V4.md` line 119. CONFIRMED.
   - The finding's "21.1 min with the memo" is actually v2's warm run. v3 with the memo took 1 298-1 526 s (21.6-25.4 min). This is a minor misattribution and does not change the point.
   - v4.1 full runs were exercised only on check112 (24 rows) and check115 (104 rows); `ACCEPTANCE_V41.md` item 4. The obs116 mutants were run with frozen v4, not v4.1. CONFIRMED.

The fix stands as proposed. Add a ROADMAP correction saying three things:
- The ≈20 min figure is v4 with the memo on, warm, on build 6118aef5, and does not apply to the permitted mode.
- The full `--no-memo` cost under v4.1 is not measured; this estimate is about 40-45 min.
- Item 1 (г) "полный" was not carried out.

Before the next ABBA seal, time one full ttl114b (or net112) run under v4.1 with `--control --no-memo` on an idle machine, then revisit the decision to stop speed work. MAJOR fits: this is not a measurement-correctness defect, but a pre-registered step was silently dropped and a program decision rests on the wrong mode's number.
